 Justice Sibo Sankar Mishra

 No. 07.10.2024
 03. Blapl No.5907 of 2024 & I.A. No.1204 of 2024

1.
Heard learned counsel for the petitioner and learned counsel for the State.

2. The petitioner is an accused in connection with E.O.W. P.S. Case No.03 of 2024 corresponding to C.T. Case No.07 of 2024 for the offences punishable under Sections 420/409/467/468/471/120-B of the IPC pending in the Court of the learned P.O. Designated Court under OPID Act, Cuttack.
The petitioner had approached the learned P.O. Designated Court under OPID Act, Cuttack praying for grant of bail.
The learned Court below vide its order dated 14.05.2024, rejected the bail application of the petitioner.
Being aggrieved, the petitioner has filed the present petition under Section 439 Cr.P.C. praying for enlargement on bail.
3. The prosecution case is that the petitioner was the Branch Head of the IDBI Bank.

During the period October, 2017 to July, 2019 it was alleged that he had committed fraud/misappropriated the Government fund to the sum of Rs.3,70,00,000/- from the Government account, which was meant for welfare activities of the people.

The said account was being maintained by the BDO, Pipli and it is alleged that without specific instructions, the amount was transferred to Ghost account and the same has been utilised by the present petitioner and another to their advantage.
On scrutiny, it was found that the amount of Rs.3.00 crores was debited and transferred to 30 loan accounts out of which twenty loan accounts were closed on deposit of interest amount in cash.
It is also alleged that Rs.70.00 lakhs was utilized in the said manner and accordingly, 35 accounts which were created fictitiously were closed with the amount received from the BDO, Pipli.
On the basis of the said allegation FIR was lodged Saroj Kanta Mohapatra vs State Of Odisha ....

4. After investigation, charge sheet was submitted on 02.07.2024 and investigation is going on.
5. Since the investigation is going on, I am not inclined to enlarge the petitioner on bail at this stage.

However, liberty is granted to the petitioner to renew his bail plea after filing of the charge sheet.
6.
With this liberty, the BLAPL is disposed of.
7. At this stage, Mr. Sarangi, learned Senior Advocate submits that he has moved an interim application for interim bail on the ground of his serious health condition.
8. Verification of health condition of the petitioner has been done.

The I.O. of the present case submitted a report dated 06.10.2024 inter alia stated as under:
"The above named patient prisoner is suffering from Chronic DVT Left lower limb.
He was referred to department of CTVs SCB MCH Cuttack on 16.05.2024 and 18.07.2024 (Copy Enclosed) for specialized treatment.
He was advised medication and colour Doppler radiological test of BL lower limb.
Colour Doppler test is done and again referred to the department of CTVs SCB MCH Cuttack on 26.09.2024 with report of colour Doppler test (Copy Enclosed).
Seen by specialized Physician and discharged with medication.
At present he is asymptomatic.

General Systemic examination are normal and taking medication regularly as per advice "
9.
Regard being had to the aforementioned report, I am of the considered view that the petitioner is required medical attention immediately.
Therefore, I am inclined to release the petitioner on interim bail for a period of two months from the date of his release.
Let the petitioner be released on interim bail for a period of two month by the learned Court in seisin over the matter on such terms and conditions as he/she may deem just and proper.
After completion of the interim bail period of two months, the petitioner shall surrender before the learned Court below.

The petitioner is directed to cooperate with the investigation and shall surrender his Passport and shall not travel beyond the jurisdiction without informing the concerned I.O.
10.
The I.A. stands disposed of.
(S.S. Mishra) Judge amit Location: HIGH COURT OF ORISSA, CUTTACK Saroj Kanta Mohapatra vs State Of Odisha .... Opp.
